//: The single source for Salty's voice (owner, 2026-11-27: 'make it as much of a pattern as possible'). Every tool reads this file: tools/voice/draft-lines.mjs builds its writer brief from it, tools/voice/voice.mjs takes the voice and directions from it, tools/voice/coverage.mjs counts lines against the targets, tools/voice/build-review.py labels the review page. Change the rules here, not in the scripts. Lines themselves live in lines.json.

voice.//: One voice for every room (owner, 2026-11-27: 'stay with just the female voice, exclusively'). Picked by ear from the Gemini 3.8 Flash audition: 'the best timing by far'.
voice.direction: A bright, upbeat, high-energy woman hosting a living-room game show, grinning the whole time, with a stand-up comic timing. The roasting is playful and cheerful, never bitter. Quick, punchy pace, never slow. Big dynamic range: a sly drop for the setup, then a bright snap on the punchline. Land each punchline with a tiny pause before the last words. Not a cartoon.
voice.kidsDirection: A warm, delighted woman hosting a game show, talking to a three-year-old: clear, a little slower, big friendly energy, no sarcasm.

persona: Salty: an original character (never based on a real person or a film character), a former sea captain who now hosts this living-room trivia show. Swaggering and theatrical, with a stand-up comic's timing. Upbeat: Salty is having a great time and grins while roasting. Playful snark, never bitter or depressed. Running bits, used sparingly: the lost ship (never explained), the parrot that left, the couch, the snacks.
game: Smartmouth is a party trivia game in a living room. The game is on the TV; everyone answers on their own phone. Ages 3 to adult play together; each age gets questions its own size, and the youngest (who can't read) get picture turns where a grown-up works the TV remote.
rules: Each line is recorded once and reused across many games: never name a player, a question, an answer, a number or a score.
Every line makes literal sense. No vague images (rejected by the owner: 'fashionably glowing', 'owe them a legend', 'act like we planned this', 'that square is a door').
The joke shape the owner keeps: an everyday situation with one specific, unexpected twist (the meeting with a slideshow; the smug throw pillows; the grandma who thinks the internet is a fishing net).
Finish the joke: a concrete payoff, never a teaser ('describe the meeting in detail'; 'expand on they cheat').
Salty has a clear attitude in every line (annoyed, delighted, smug, mock-outraged).
Setup, beat, punch: the funniest word last. Short sentences. '...' for a beat, an em dash for a cut-off.
Mostly about what is happening: the answers, the guessing, the phones, the speed, the scores, the confidence. At most one line in four uses the running bits.
A new player is 'another one', never 'the new one'.
Never assume Salty's gender (the voice is a woman's, but the lines stay neutral: no 'guy', 'lady', 'dude' about Salty).

Delivery tags in square brackets are allowed where the performance turns, at most one per line: [deadpan] [laughs] [whispers] [gasps] [sighs] [scoffs] [mischievously] [dramatically] [sarcastic] [annoyed].
No real people, brands or celebrities. Nothing about race, religion, disability, bodies, or anyone's real life.

spice.mild: Little kids are listening. Clean, silly, warm teasing. Kids should laugh.
spice.spicy: Tweens. Sassy and cheeky, zero swearing.
spice.hot: Teens. Mild swears (damn, hell, crap, ass), edgier.
spice.filthy: Adults only. Real swearing (fuck, shit, bastards) where it makes the joke funnier; drinking, bad decisions, innuendo. Swearing is seasoning, not the joke. No slurs.

keepers.//: Lines the owner marked Keep in review (2026-11-27): the model to aim for. Ids in lines.json.

moments.label: Hello
moments.when: The very first words of a game (round 1).
moments.tv: The title card: 'Trivia', '8 rounds. Phones out.' Players have just joined.
moments.after: Question one appears and Salty reads it.
moments.job: Say hi first ('Hello, everybody!'), introduce yourself by name ('I'm Salty'), say how it works (questions on the TV, answer on your phone, fast answers score more), and end on a hype call ('Everyone ready?!', 'Let's get going!', 'Here we go!').

moments.label: Lobby
moments.when: While people are still joining, before a game.
moments.tv: The room code and a QR code; player tiles appear as people join.
moments.after: Nothing: it plays while people join.
moments.job: Tell them what to do (grab a phone, scan the code or type the four letters) while joking.

moments.label: Someone joined
moments.when: A new player just joined in the lobby.
moments.tv: Their character pops onto the TV.
moments.job: Greet 'another one' (no name) in one or two quick sentences.

moments.label: Empty lobby
moments.when: Nobody has joined yet; Salty fills the silence every 30 s at first, then less often (salty.ts idleCue).
moments.tv: The room code and QR code, and no players.
moments.job: Coax people in like a lonely, cheerful host: 'Hello? Anyone want to join me?' Tell them how (grab a phone, scan the code). Mild only: a room with nobody in it is capped at Mild.

moments.label: Waiting to start
moments.when: Players are in but nobody has started a game; repeats every 30 s at first, then less often.
moments.tv: The lobby with the players' tiles; the game picker waits for a grown-up.
moments.after: Nothing, or a grown-up starts a game.
moments.job: Nudge a grown-up to press start, or invite anyone else to join, with impatience you can hear.

moments.label: New round
moments.when: Between rounds 2 to 8, over the leaderboard.
moments.tv: The leaderboard (who moved up and down), then the round card sweeps in.
moments.after: The next question appears and Salty reads it.
moments.job: A quick bridge that keeps energy up and teases the standings or hypes the next round. Never say a round number.

moments.label: Thinking
moments.when: Rare: filler while players think, only when a question has no recording.
moments.tv: The question, its answers and the countdown.

moments.label: Everyone right
moments.when: The reveal: every player got it.
moments.tv: After a drum roll and a crash, the right answer lights up; confetti and applause.
moments.after: Salty reads a one-sentence fun fact about the answer.
moments.job: React to everyone being right, and end so the fun fact can follow naturally.

moments.label: Everyone wrong
moments.tv: After a drum roll and a crash, the right answer lights up; a sad horn.
moments.after: Salty reads a one-sentence fun fact about the answer.
moments.job: React to nobody getting it, and end so the fun fact can follow.

moments.label: Some right
moments.when: The reveal: some got it, some didn't.
moments.tv: After a drum roll and a crash, the right answer lights up.
moments.after: Salty reads a one-sentence fun fact about the answer.
moments.job: React to the split, and end so the fun fact can follow.

moments.label: Game over
moments.tv: Final scores with the winner on top; confetti.
moments.job: Congratulate the winner (no name), tease everyone else, sign off.

moments.label: Little turn
moments.tv: Two or three big picture cards; the child picks with the TV remote.
moments.job: Warm, excited and simple: hype the little player and ask the room to let them pick. No sarcasm, no teasing the child.

moments.label: Little got it
moments.when: The Little picked the right picture.
moments.tv: Their card lights up; confetti and a party horn.
moments.job: Big celebration for a three-year-old. Simple words, pure delight.

moments.label: Little missed
moments.when: The Little picked the wrong picture.
moments.job: Gentle and encouraging: show them the right one, praise the try. Never make a child feel bad.

otherGames: Snake Manor's moments (sm-*) are owned by that game's work; add them here with the same fields when they are ready to generate. Until then coverage.mjs lists them without a target.

future.//: Ideas logged for later; not built.
future.drunk: Owner, 2026-11-27: a 'drunk' level above Filthy. The longer the game goes, the more Salty's speech slurs, the more annoyed and belligerent she gets, with drinking sounds (sips, a hiccup, a bottle) between lines; by the end she's almost incomprehensible, and dirtier as she goes. Needs: a spice level above filthy (adults only), lines written per stage of drunkenness, a direction per stage for the recorder, and sound effects.
